units.title: Challenges
units.intro: Grammar: finite and non-finite clauses, and understanding complex sentences.

cards.title: Finite and non-finite clauses
rule: A **finite clause** has a verb that shows tense and agrees with a subject: *She **faces** many challenges.* *Because he **was** ill, ...*

A **non-finite clause** has no tense; its verb is a **to-infinitive**, an **-ing participle** or a **past participle**: ***To succeed**, you must work hard.* ***Facing** many problems, she never gave up.* ***Given** enough time, we can solve it.*
The subject of a participle clause must be the same as the main clause subject: *Walking home, **I** saw an accident* (I was walking).

examples.text: Having finished the exam, she went home.
Walking to school, the rain started.
examples.fix: Walking to school, I was caught in the rain.

examples.text: To pass the exam, you need to revise.

cards.title: Step-by-step
cards.problem: Which of the following sentences exhibits the correct English word order (S-V-O)?

steps.text: **Step 1: Look at the sentence.** English requires a strict Subject-Verb-Object (S-V-O) pattern.
The subject is 'The security guard', the verb is 'locked', and the direct object is 'the main gate'.

**Step 2: Watch out for the trap.** Option A and Option C place the verb ('locked') at the end of the clause, which is an S-O-V pattern typical of Tigrinya grammar (ሓላው ሰላም ማዕጾ ዓጸዎ) and represents a common translation from Tigrinya error.

cards.answer: The security guard locked the main gate at midnight.

cards.title: Step-by-step
cards.problem: Which sentence is missing a linking verb (is/am/are/was/were)?

steps.text: **Step 1: Look at the sentence.** Every English sentence expressing a state of being requires a linking verb ('is', 'are', 'was', 'were') between the subject and the word that describes the subject.
**Step 2: Watch out for the trap.** In Option C, the linking verb 'is' is completely missing.

In Tigrinya, the linking verb can sometimes be omitted or structurally merged, leading students to translate "ሓወይ ኣብቲ ዓዲ ትጉህ ሓረስታይ [እዩ]" directly as "My brother a hardworking farmer..." without including the linking verb 'is'.

cards.answer: My brother a hardworking farmer in the village.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: Choose the sentence that correctly manages sentence boundaries without creating a comma splice.

options.A: The rain was heavy, we decided to stay indoors.
options.B: The rain was heavy we decided to stay indoors.
options.C: The rain was heavy; therefore, we decided to stay indoors.
options.D: Because the rain was heavy, so we decided to stay indoors.

cards.why:
**Step 1: Look at the sentence**
A comma splice occurs when two independent clauses are joined with only a comma. Option A is a comma splice. Option B is a run-on sentence. Option C uses a semicolon and a conjunctive adverb ('therefore'), which is structurally perfect.

**Step 2: Watch out for the trap**
Option D is a double-conjunction error ('Because... so...'). Tigrinya speakers often use both because they translate word endings like "ስለዝ-... ስለዚ..." directly into English. Option C correctly separates the clauses.

**Step 3: In Tigrinya**
ክልተ ናጻ ዝኾኑ ምሉእ ሓሳባት (independent clauses) ብኮማ ጥራይ ከተኣሳሰሩ ኣይኽእሉን እዮም (እዚ Comma Splice ይበሃል)። ኣብ Option C ዝተጠቐስናሉ ሰሚኮለን (;) ንሰንሰለት ምሉእ ሓሳብ ብግቡእ ይዓጽዎ። Option D ድማ 'Because' ን 'so' ን ብሓባር ብምጥቃም ዝተገብረ ልሙድ ናይ ትርጉም ጌጋ እዩ።

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: Complete the sentence with the correct word order: 'The school principal ________.'

options.A: yesterday welcomed the new students warmly
options.B: warmly welcomed the new students yesterday
options.C: welcomed yesterday warmly the new students
options.D: the new students welcomed warmly yesterday

cards.why:
**Step 1: Look at the sentence**
English adverbs of manner ('warmly') usually precede the main verb or follow the object. Adverbs of time ('yesterday') belong at the end of the sentence. The correct structure is: Subject ('The school principal') + Adverb of Manner ('warmly') + Verb ('welcomed') + Object ('the new students') + Adverb of Time ('yesterday').

**Step 2: Watch out for the trap**
Option D shows S-O-V word order. Option A places the time adverb ('yesterday') between the subject and the verb, which is acceptable in Tigrinya but highly irregular and awkward in English unless formatted as a fronted adverbial.

**Step 3: In Tigrinya**
ኣብ እንግሊዘኛ ናይ ግዜ ተወሳኺ ሓበሬታ (Adverb of Time - 'yesterday') ወትሩ ኣብ መወዳእታ ምሉእ ሓሳብ ክስራዕ ከሎ፡ ናይ ኣገባብ ተወሳኺ ሓበሬታ (Adverb of Manner - 'warmly') ድማ ቅድሚ እቲ ዋና ግሲ ይመጽእ። Option B ነዚ ናይ S-V-O ስርዓት ብትኽክል ዝሓለወ እዩ።

cards.title: Quick check
cards.why:
**Step 1:** A finite clause has a verb showing tense with a subject.

**Step 2:** "the road was closed" has a subject and past tense.

**Step 3:** The others are to-infinitive, perfect participle and past participle clauses.

**Tip:** A finite clause has a verb that shows tense and agrees with a subject; a non-finite clause uses to-infinitive, -ing or -ed forms. In long sentences, find the main subject and main verb first.

cards.title: Understanding long sentences
rule: To understand a long sentence: (1) find the **main clause** (subject + finite verb); (2) put brackets around subordinate and non-finite clauses; (3) ask what each bracket adds (time, reason, condition, purpose).

examples.text: [Although tired,] the farmers [working in the fields] continued.
Main clause here: the farmers continued.

cards.title: Unit summary
body: Finite clauses have a tensed verb and a subject; non-finite clauses use to-infinitives, -ing or past participles and borrow their subject from the main clause. To read complex sentences, find the main clause first.

cards.title: Break down a long sentence
cards.problem: Find the main subject, main verb and the main message of: "The young engineer, who had grown up in a village without electricity and had studied by candlelight for years, designed a solar lamp that now lights thousands of homes."

steps.text: **Step 1: Remove the relative clause.** Cut "who had grown up in a village without electricity and had studied by candlelight for years" (it only describes the engineer).
**Step 2: Find the core.** "The young engineer designed a solar lamp." Subject: the young engineer; main verb: designed.
**Step 3: Look at what is left.** "that now lights thousands of homes" describes the lamp.
**Step 4: State the message.** An engineer from a poor village invented a solar lamp that is now widely used.

cards.answer: Subject: the young engineer; main verb: designed; message: he invented a solar lamp now used in thousands of homes.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: My father, having put on his jacket and ______ his breakfast left for office.
cards.why: The sentence uses a perfect participle clause ('having' + V3). Because 'put' and the missing verb are part of the same structure, the second verb must also be a past participle (V3).

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: What is the main verb? "The plan that the committee presented after months of discussion with farmers and officials was finally accepted."
cards.why:
**Step 1:** Remove "that the committee presented after months of discussion with farmers and officials".

**Step 2:** The core is "The plan was finally accepted".

**Step 3:** The main verb is "was accepted" (passive).

**Tip:** A finite clause has a verb that shows tense and agrees with a subject; a non-finite clause uses to-infinitive, -ing or -ed forms. In long sentences, find the main subject and main verb first.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: In "Students wishing to join the club should register by Friday", what is the subject?

options.A: Students wishing to join the club

cards.why:
**Step 1:** "wishing to join the club" is a participle phrase that belongs to "Students".

**Step 2:** The whole noun phrase is the subject of "should register".

**Step 3:** Answer: Students wishing to join the club.

**Tip:** A finite clause has a verb that shows tense and agrees with a subject; a non-finite clause uses to-infinitive, -ing or -ed forms. In long sentences, find the main subject and main verb first.
